title: Two paths
summary: The poem compares a person who follows God’s teaching with windblown chaff.
meaning: The rooted tree pictures steady growth. Chaff pictures a life without lasting support.

title: Kings oppose the Lord’s chosen king
summary: Rulers resist the Lord and his anointed king. The poem calls them to serve with care.
meaning: Royal power remains answerable to God. Defiance cannot secure the rulers’ future.

title: Rest while enemies surround the speaker
summary: The speaker faces many enemies but sleeps with trust in God’s protection.
meaning: Rest becomes an act of trust during danger. The heading connects the prayer with Absalom’s rebellion.

title: An evening prayer for peace
summary: The speaker asks for an answer, challenges falsehood, and lies down in peace.
meaning: The poem contrasts inward joy with the security people seek in harvests.

title: A morning prayer for guidance
summary: The speaker asks God to hear and lead. Deceitful enemies threaten the path ahead.
meaning: The request joins worship with a need for clear direction among harmful voices.

title: A prayer through tears
summary: The speaker asks for mercy during weakness, fear, and sleepless grief.
meaning: The closing confidence follows tears. It does not remove the pain described earlier.

title: A plea for a fair judgment
summary: The speaker offers to accept judgment if guilty. The prayer asks God to stop violence.
meaning: The poem places the speaker’s conduct under examination along with the enemies’ conduct.

title: Human life beneath the stars
summary: The speaker marvels at the heavens and humanity’s place among God’s works.
meaning: Smallness does not erase human worth. Care for other creatures carries responsibility.

title: Praise for justice against oppression
summary: The speaker praises God’s judgment and asks for help against enemies.
meaning: The poor may seem forgotten, but the poem insists their hope still matters.

title: Why does the oppressor seem safe?
summary: The speaker describes hidden attacks on the poor and asks God to intervene.
meaning: The prayer challenges the belief that unseen harm escapes judgment.

title: Trust when the foundations fail
summary: Others urge flight. The speaker looks to the Lord, who sees human conduct.
meaning: Danger raises the question of where trust belongs when familiar supports collapse.

title: Help when honest speech disappears
summary: The speaker contrasts flattery and boastful words with God’s promise to protect the poor.
meaning: Words can conceal harm or offer protection. The poem asks which voices deserve trust.

title: How long must the speaker wait?
summary: The speaker asks how long God will remain distant, then recalls his kindness.
meaning: Waiting and trust occupy the same short prayer. Trust does not prevent the question.

title: Corruption and the hope of rescue
summary: The poem describes widespread wrongdoing and people who consume others without concern.
meaning: The final hope turns toward rescue for Israel rather than confidence in human goodness.

title: Who may stay in God’s presence?
summary: The poem names honesty, fair dealings, and refusal to exploit others.
meaning: Worship requires conduct that protects neighbors, not simply entry into a holy place.

title: A secure portion
summary: The speaker rejects other gods and finds security in the Lord’s counsel and presence.
meaning: Inheritance becomes an image of belonging. The speaker’s greatest good is closeness to God.

title: A plea for protection from violent people
summary: The speaker asks God to examine the heart and shelter it from enemies.
meaning: The prayer seeks protection while inviting scrutiny of the speaker’s own conduct.

title: Rescue pictured through storm and battle
summary: The speaker recalls God’s rescue through earthquake, storm, and strength against enemies.
meaning: Large images give form to deliverance. The heading connects the song with David and Saul.

title: The heavens and God’s teaching
summary: The skies declare God’s glory. His teaching guides the speaker toward honest words and thoughts.
meaning: The poem moves from the visible world to the conduct of one person.

title: A prayer for the king before danger
summary: The people ask God to accept the king’s offerings and answer his plans.
meaning: Chariots and horses represent strength, but the people place their trust in God.

title: Thanks for the king’s deliverance
summary: The poem celebrates the king’s joy, life, honor, and rescue from enemies.
meaning: Royal success appears as a gift requiring gratitude rather than a private achievement.

title: Abandonment, suffering, and praise
summary: The speaker cries about distance, mockery, and physical danger. The ending calls others to praise.
meaning: The prayer changes from isolation to shared praise. The painful opening remains part of its witness.

title: The Lord as shepherd and host
summary: The speaker describes guidance, danger, welcome, and a place in the Lord’s house.
meaning: The shepherd’s care continues through the dark valley. The poem does not promise a path without danger.

title: Who may enter before the King of glory?
summary: The poem asks who may approach God. Its final call welcomes the King of glory.
meaning: Clean hands and a truthful heart connect worship with daily conduct.

title: Guidance, forgiveness, and loneliness
summary: The speaker asks God to teach, forgive earlier sins, and relieve distress.
meaning: Learning requires humility. The request for guidance includes an honest account of past failures.

title: Integrity and love for worship
summary: The speaker asks God to examine the heart and refuses fellowship with harmful people.
meaning: The claim of integrity becomes a request for examination rather than freedom from scrutiny.

title: Seeking God’s face amid fear
summary: The speaker wants to dwell near God and asks for help against enemies.
meaning: Confidence and pleading stand together. Waiting requires courage while danger remains.

title: Do not remain silent
summary: The speaker asks God to hear and avoid judging him with deceitful people.
meaning: The prayer ends by asking God to shepherd the whole people, beyond one person’s need.

title: The Lord’s voice over the storm
summary: The poem describes the Lord’s voice shaking waters, trees, mountains, and wilderness.
meaning: The powerful storm ends with a blessing of peace for the people.

title: Mourning becomes dancing
summary: The speaker recalls rescue from death, a time of confidence, and renewed praise.
meaning: Prosperity once seemed secure. Loss taught the speaker to recognize dependence on God.

title: Entrusting life to God
summary: The speaker describes traps, shame, and rejection while asking for refuge.
meaning: Entrusting the spirit to God accompanies an appeal for help, not withdrawal from trouble.

title: Confession after the weight of silence
summary: The speaker describes the strain of hiding sin and the relief of confession.
meaning: The poem connects forgiveness with honesty. Concealment had increased the speaker’s distress.

title: Praise for the maker who sees all people
summary: The poem celebrates creation and God’s knowledge of human hearts.
meaning: Armies and strength cannot guarantee rescue. Hope rests in the Lord’s care.

title: Learning to seek peace
summary: The speaker praises rescue and calls others to truthful speech, goodness, and peace.
meaning: Deliverance leads to practical teaching. Nearness to the brokenhearted remains central to the promise.

title: A plea against false accusations
summary: The speaker asks for defense against enemies who repay care with hostility.
meaning: The prayer names the wound of betrayal as well as the threat of physical harm.

title: Wickedness and the reach of kindness
summary: The poem contrasts inward wrongdoing with God’s kindness, faithfulness, and care for living creatures.
meaning: Human deceit appears narrow beside the wide reach of God’s protection.

title: Do not envy the success of wrongdoing
summary: The poem urges patience, generosity, and trust when harmful people seem to prosper.
meaning: Its advice asks readers to choose lasting goodness over the attraction of immediate success.

title: Pain, guilt, and distant friends
summary: The speaker describes illness, wrongdoing, and companions standing far away.
meaning: The prayer joins bodily pain with guilt and loneliness. It asks God not to withdraw too.

title: The brevity of life
summary: The speaker struggles to remain silent and reflects on how quickly human life passes.
meaning: Short life makes wealth uncertain. The prayer asks where hope can rest.

title: Rescue followed by a new appeal
summary: The speaker recalls rescue and public praise, then asks for help in fresh distress.
meaning: Earlier deliverance becomes a reason to pray again when new trouble arrives.

title: Care for the weak and betrayal
summary: The speaker praises care for the poor and asks for help amid illness and betrayal.
meaning: The kindness praised at the start contrasts with the companions’ conduct toward the suffering speaker.

title: Thirst for God far from worship
summary: The speaker remembers worship, hears taunts, and longs for God like a thirsty deer.
meaning: Remembered joy deepens the sense of distance. The repeated call to hope answers inward despair.

title: Send light and truth
summary: The speaker asks for defense and a return to God’s altar.
meaning: The repeated question to the soul connects this prayer with Psalm 42’s struggle for hope.

title: A people ask why defeat came
summary: The people recall earlier victories but describe present shame despite continued loyalty.
meaning: The prayer questions a simple link between faithfulness and immediate success.

title: A song for a royal wedding
summary: The poem praises a king’s rule and addresses the bride entering his household.
meaning: The wedding song joins royal honor with the demand that the king love justice.

title: Refuge when the world shakes
summary: The poem pictures mountains falling, nations raging, and God protecting his city.
meaning: The call to be still interrupts panic and draws attention to God’s rule.

title: Praise before the king of all nations
summary: The poem calls every people to celebrate God’s rule.
meaning: The praise reaches beyond Israel. The rulers of the earth belong under one greater authority.

title: Walk around Zion
summary: The people praise God’s city and tell the next generation about its towers and defenses.
meaning: The walk turns a visible city into a shared memory of protection.

title: Wealth cannot purchase life
summary: The poem contrasts the confidence of wealthy people with the death that reaches everyone.
meaning: Possessions cannot redeem another person’s life. The final warning asks what riches actually secure.

title: God examines the worshipers
summary: God calls the people to account and challenges offerings joined with theft and harmful speech.
meaning: Thanksgiving and honest conduct matter more than treating sacrifices as payment for God’s care.

title: Create a clean heart
summary: The speaker confesses wrongdoing and asks for cleansing, renewed joy, and a willing spirit.
meaning: The request reaches beyond escape from punishment toward a changed heart.

title: A powerful person’s harmful words
summary: The poem condemns deceit and trust in riches. The speaker appears as an olive tree.
meaning: Destructive speech exposes misplaced confidence. The living tree represents trust in enduring kindness.

title: Corruption and rescue for Israel
summary: The poem describes widespread wrongdoing and the fear of those who oppose God’s people.
meaning: Its closing hope seeks the restoration of Israel rather than praising human strength.

title: Help against strangers and violent people
summary: The speaker asks God to hear, defend, and sustain life.
meaning: The heading connects the prayer with the Ziphites reporting David’s hiding place to Saul.

title: Betrayal by a close companion
summary: The speaker longs to escape violence and describes betrayal by a trusted companion.
meaning: Shared worship makes the betrayal especially painful. The prayer seeks support beyond the failed friendship.

title: Trust amid fear
summary: The speaker describes pursuit, twisted words, and tears while declaring trust in God.
meaning: Fear is admitted before trust is expressed. The poem treats tears as worth remembering.

title: Shelter until danger passes
summary: The speaker seeks refuge while describing traps and hostile people.
meaning: The prayer moves from danger toward praise without pretending the threats were harmless.

title: A cry against unjust rulers
summary: The speaker challenges corrupt judgment and asks God to overthrow violent people.
meaning: The harsh images express anger at injustice. They show the force of the speaker’s demand.

title: Enemies circle the house
summary: The speaker describes enemies prowling like dogs and turns toward God as a refuge.
meaning: The heading connects the threat with Saul’s men watching David’s house.

title: Defeat and a renewed appeal
summary: The people describe shaken land and ask God to help against their enemies.
meaning: The named lands appear in a plea for renewed strength, not a travel account.

title: A prayer from far away
summary: The speaker asks for shelter beneath God’s wings and protection for the king.
meaning: Distance becomes a reason to seek a refuge stronger than the speaker’s own position.

title: Waiting without depending on riches
summary: The speaker rejects falsehood, oppression, and trust in wealth while waiting for God.
meaning: Silence expresses settled reliance. The poem joins power with kindness and accountability.

title: Longing for God in dry land
summary: The speaker seeks God, remembers worship, and praises during the night.
meaning: Dry land gives a physical image to longing. Memory sustains praise while the need remains.

title: Hidden plots and harmful speech
summary: The speaker compares hostile words with arrows and describes secret plans against the innocent.
meaning: The poem expects hidden attacks to become visible through God’s judgment.

title: Praise for forgiveness and harvest
summary: The poem thanks God for answered prayer, calm seas, rain, and abundant crops.
meaning: Care for the land connects worship with the food that sustains ordinary life.

title: A people remember rescue
summary: The people recall passage through water, testing, and deliverance. One speaker tells of answered prayer.
meaning: Shared memory leads into personal witness. Both describe help received after hardship.

title: Blessing that reaches the nations
summary: The people ask for blessing so every nation may know God’s way.
meaning: The harvest becomes a reason for the whole earth to give thanks.

title: The protector leads his people
summary: The poem pictures God advancing, scattering enemies, and providing for people without protection.
meaning: Praise connects great power with care for orphans, widows, and prisoners.

title: Sinking beneath shame and hostility
summary: The speaker compares distress with deep water and asks for rescue from hatred.
meaning: The prayer gives voice to isolation and anger. Its demands against enemies require careful reading.

title: An urgent call for help
summary: The speaker asks God to hurry and stop enemies. Those who seek him should rejoice.
meaning: The short prayer keeps urgency at its center. The speaker has no resources to delay.

title: A prayer in old age
summary: The speaker recalls trust from youth and asks for help while strength fails.
meaning: Old age becomes a time to tell the next generation about God’s help.

title: A king who protects the poor
summary: The prayer asks for a king who judges fairly and rescues the weak from oppression.
meaning: Good rule receives its measure from the safety of those who lack power.

title: Envy challenged in the sanctuary
summary: The speaker envies wicked people’s comfort. Worship changes the view of their future.
meaning: The poem admits the attraction of easy success before finding a different measure of good.

title: A plea after the sanctuary’s destruction
summary: The people describe burned worship places and ask God to remember his people.
meaning: The prayer joins damaged buildings with the fear that God has withdrawn from the community.

title: A warning against proud power
summary: The poem gives thanks and warns arrogant people that judgment belongs to God.
meaning: Raised horns picture claims to strength. The warning challenges power that refuses restraint.

title: God stops the weapons of war
summary: The poem praises God in Zion and describes warriors losing their strength.
meaning: Divine judgment protects the afflicted while ending the confidence of armed power.

title: Remembering rescue during a sleepless night
summary: The speaker asks whether God’s kindness has ended, then remembers the passage through the sea.
meaning: Memory does not erase the questions. It provides another way to see the present silence.

title: Tell the children about earlier failures
summary: The poem recalls the wilderness, repeated rebellion, and God’s choice of Judah and David.
meaning: The long account asks the next generation to learn rather than repeat the same failures.

title: Prayer among the ruins of Jerusalem
summary: The people describe destroyed worship places, unburied bodies, and hostile neighbors.
meaning: Grief leads to requests for forgiveness, rescue, and judgment against those who caused the destruction.

title: Restore the vine you brought from Egypt
summary: The people ask God to restore them and compare Israel with a damaged vine.
meaning: The vine once spread widely. Its broken defenses picture a people exposed to attack.

title: Listen to the voice that freed you
summary: The poem calls for festival music and recalls God’s rescue from Egypt.
meaning: The warning says freedom should lead to listening rather than continued refusal.

title: God judges the assembly
summary: God confronts judges who fail the poor. He orders them to protect people facing harm.
meaning: McClellan reads the accused figures as other gods failing to govern their nations justly.

title: A prayer against surrounding enemies
summary: The speaker lists hostile peoples and asks God to defeat their united plans.
meaning: Memories of earlier victories become the language for a present plea for protection.

title: Longing for God’s courts
summary: The speaker envies birds nesting near the altar and describes the joy of approaching worship.
meaning: The journey’s hardship stands beside the desire for one day near God.

title: A people ask for renewed life
summary: The people remember forgiveness, ask for restoration, and picture kindness meeting truth.
meaning: Peace includes justice. The poem joins renewed life with a changed relationship to God.

title: A plea from a faithful servant
summary: The speaker asks for mercy, an undivided heart, and a sign of help.
meaning: The prayer links rescue with learning to walk in God’s truth.

title: Peoples counted as belonging to Zion
summary: The poem names foreign peoples and imagines them registered as born in Zion.
meaning: The birth register widens belonging beyond one people’s ancestry. Rahab here names Egypt poetically.

title: A prayer that ends in darkness
summary: The speaker describes isolation, approaching death, and repeated unanswered cries.
meaning: The final line offers no turn toward relief. The prayer preserves suffering without a quick resolution.

title: A promise to David amid royal defeat
summary: The poem praises God’s rule and promise to David, then describes the king’s humiliation.
meaning: The question asks how lasting promises fit a broken crown and unanswered distress.

title: Teach us to number our days
summary: The prayer contrasts God’s enduring life with brief human years and asks for renewed kindness.
meaning: Awareness of limited time leads to a request for wisdom and useful work.

title: Shelter under God’s wings
summary: The poem describes protection from traps, disease, terror, and attacking forces.
meaning: Its images express confident trust. They belong to a song rather than a prediction for every life.

title: A Sabbath song of lasting growth
summary: The poem praises God’s works and contrasts fleeting wicked success with fruitful old age.
meaning: Trees near God’s house picture a life that keeps bearing fruit beyond youth.

title: The king above the flood
summary: The poem pictures God’s enduring rule above the roar of great waters.
meaning: The threatening flood gives scale to a greater stability in God’s reign.

title: Justice for people harmed by rulers
summary: The speaker condemns rulers who kill people without protection and calls for judgment.
meaning: The poem names harmful laws as well as harmful acts. Legal power does not make injustice right.

title: Praise without a hardened heart
summary: The people approach God with singing, then hear a warning from the wilderness story.
meaning: Worship must include listening. Earlier refusal becomes a warning for the present gathering.

title: Tell the nations about the Lord
summary: The poem calls the earth to sing and all peoples to recognize God’s rule.
meaning: The coming judgment is cause for joy because it promises fairness for the world.

title: Light for those who love justice
summary: The poem pictures clouds, fire, trembling earth, and joy at God’s reign.
meaning: The call to hate evil turns praise into a choice about conduct.

title: A new song for rescue
summary: The people celebrate deliverance with voices and instruments. Rivers and hills join the praise.
meaning: The widening celebration connects Israel’s rescue with fair judgment for the whole earth.

title: A holy ruler who answers
summary: The poem praises justice and recalls Moses, Aaron, and Samuel calling on God.
meaning: Answered prayer includes both forgiveness and correction. Holiness does not remove accountability.

title: Enter with thanks
summary: The people approach God with joyful service and praise his lasting kindness.
meaning: The short invitation grounds gratitude in belonging and care across generations.

title: A ruler’s promises for his household
summary: The speaker promises honest conduct and refuses deceit, slander, and proud company.
meaning: Fair rule begins with the choices made close to home, not only public promises.

title: An afflicted person waits for Zion’s renewal
summary: The speaker describes weakness and loneliness while hoping for restored worship in Jerusalem.
meaning: A brief human life is set beside God’s endurance and hope for later generations.

title: Remember mercy and human frailty
summary: The speaker recalls forgiveness, healing, and kindness while comparing human life with grass.
meaning: Awareness of weakness supports compassion rather than contempt for those who fail.

title: A world supplied with life
summary: The poem describes water, food, animals, seasons, work, and God’s renewing breath.
meaning: Many kinds of life depend on provision beyond their own strength.

title: Remember the promise and the journey
summary: The poem recalls Abraham’s family, Joseph in Egypt, Moses, and the departure from slavery.
meaning: The long memory connects the gift of land with a call to keep God’s teaching.

title: Confession through the people’s history
summary: The people confess failures during the wilderness and later life in the land.
meaning: Remembering wrongdoing becomes part of asking for rescue. The account includes harm to children.

title: Give thanks after different kinds of danger
summary: The poem describes lost travelers, prisoners, sick people, and sailors finding rescue.
meaning: Different situations share a repeated call to recognize kindness after help arrives.

title: Praise followed by a plea for victory
summary: The speaker praises God and asks for help across named lands.
meaning: The images of land concern rule and conflict. They do not describe a new journey.

title: Anger against an accuser
summary: The speaker describes hatred repaying kindness and calls for severe punishment of an enemy.
meaning: The prayer records intense anger. Its wishes extend harm to the enemy’s family.

title: A royal figure and a priest
summary: The poem addresses a ruler seated at God’s right hand and names Melchizedek’s priestly order.
meaning: Royal and priestly images stand together. Later readers apply them to the Messiah.

title: Remember the works of the Lord
summary: The poem celebrates provision, faithfulness, and teaching that endures.
meaning: Remembered help leads toward wisdom expressed in keeping God’s commands.

title: Generosity in a secure household
summary: The poem praises the person who fears God, lends freely, and gives to the poor.
meaning: Its picture of strength includes generosity. Security does not require withholding help from neighbors.

title: The high God lifts the lowly
summary: The poem praises the Lord above the nations and describes poor people raised from dust.
meaning: Greatness appears through attention to people others overlook.

title: The earth responds to the departure from Egypt
summary: The sea flees, the Jordan turns back, and mountains move before the Lord.
meaning: The landscape becomes a poetic witness to the people’s rescue and God’s provision of water.

title: Living trust and lifeless idols
summary: The people ask God to defend his name and contrast his power with handmade idols.
meaning: The idols have body parts but cannot act. Trust shapes what worshipers become like.

title: Thanks after a plea near death
summary: The speaker recalls crying for help and promises public thanks and fulfilled vows.
meaning: Rescue leads to gratitude expressed before others, not only private relief.

title: Every nation is called to praise
summary: The poem calls all peoples to praise the Lord’s kindness and faithfulness.
meaning: Its two verses widen the invitation beyond Israel while keeping the reason for praise clear.

title: The rejected stone becomes central
summary: The speaker celebrates rescue and enters the gates of worship with thanks.
meaning: Rejection does not settle the stone’s worth. Deliverance changes its place in the community.

title: Learning God’s teaching through a long prayer
summary: The speaker asks for understanding, protection, and faithfulness while facing hardship.
meaning: Its 22 sections follow Hebrew alphabet letters. Each section has eight verses about God’s teaching.

title: Peace among people who seek war
summary: The speaker asks for rescue from lying tongues and describes living among hostile people.
meaning: Meshech and Kedar express distance and hostility. The poem does not give a travel sequence.

title: Help from the maker of heaven and earth
summary: The speaker looks toward the hills and hears assurance of God’s watchful care.
meaning: The keeper’s wakefulness answers the traveler’s need for protection along the way.

title: Prayer for Jerusalem’s peace
summary: The speaker rejoices in entering Jerusalem and asks for peace within its walls.
meaning: Love for the city includes concern for the people who live and worship there.

title: A plea from people treated with contempt
summary: The people look to God as servants watch their master’s hand.
meaning: The image joins dependence with expectation. The prayer names contempt as a burden needing relief.

title: What if the Lord had not helped?
summary: The people compare danger with flood and a bird’s trap, then celebrate escape.
meaning: The imagined outcome makes rescue visible by describing what could have overwhelmed them.

title: Steadfast trust and crooked paths
summary: The poem compares those who trust God with Mount Zion surrounded by mountains.
meaning: The closing prayer asks for good treatment while warning against joining harmful conduct.

title: Restoration and tears at planting
summary: The people remember sudden joy and ask for further renewal like streams in dry land.
meaning: Planting with tears keeps hope connected to effort made before any harvest appears.

title: Work, rest, and children
summary: The poem says building and guarding depend on God and describes children as a gift.
meaning: The contrast challenges anxious labor that leaves no room for rest or trust.

title: Blessing at the household table
summary: The poem pictures fruitful work, a spouse, children, and peace for Jerusalem.
meaning: Household well-being connects with the wider community rather than remaining a private good.

title: A people remember repeated oppression
summary: The people describe long mistreatment and compare it with plowing across their backs.
meaning: The image gives physical force to oppression. Survival does not make the earlier harm small.

title: Waiting from the depths
summary: The speaker cries for mercy and waits for God like guards waiting for morning.
meaning: Hope rests in forgiveness rather than a claim to have avoided every wrong.

title: A quieted soul
summary: The speaker rejects proud aims and compares the soul with a weaned child.
meaning: The child’s settled presence pictures trust without demands for greater status.

title: Remember David’s promise about worship
summary: The prayer recalls David seeking a place for the ark and God’s promise about Zion.
meaning: Royal promise and worship belong together. The prayer also asks for faithful descendants and joyful priests.

title: The goodness of living together
summary: The poem compares unity with flowing oil and dew reaching Zion.
meaning: The descending images picture a blessing shared rather than kept at its source.

title: Blessing in the night
summary: The poem calls servants in the Lord’s house to praise during the night.
meaning: The brief exchange joins the worshipers’ blessing of God with a blessing sent from Zion.

title: Praise above idols and earthly rulers
summary: The poem remembers rescue from Egypt, defeated kings, and God’s rule over nature.
meaning: The remembered acts contrast with idols that cannot speak, see, or hear.

title: Kindness remembered in every line
summary: The poem recalls creation, departure from Egypt, wilderness travel, and provision of food.
meaning: The repeated response connects each remembered act with enduring kindness.

title: Songs withheld beside Babylon’s rivers
summary: Exiles remember Zion, resist demands for songs, and end with a violent wish against Babylon.
meaning: The final wish includes killing children. It expresses revenge within the exiles’ grief and humiliation.

title: Thanks before the mighty
summary: The speaker gives thanks for an answer and says God attends to the lowly.
meaning: Confidence about rescue stands beside a final request not to abandon the work already begun.

title: Known wherever the speaker goes
summary: The speaker describes God’s knowledge, inescapable presence, and care before birth.
meaning: The final request invites examination of the heart after forceful words against enemies.

title: Protection from violent people
summary: The speaker asks for rescue from traps, hostile words, and plans for war.
meaning: The closing confidence turns toward justice for the poor and safety for upright people.

title: Guard the mouth and guide correction
summary: The speaker asks for careful speech and welcomes correction from an upright person.
meaning: Protection includes help against the speaker’s own harmful choices, not only outside enemies.

title: A refuge when nobody offers help
summary: The speaker describes hidden traps, failed escape, and the absence of anyone who cares.
meaning: The prayer names abandonment directly and asks for release into a grateful gathering.

title: Teach me the way I should go
summary: The speaker admits no living person is fully just and asks for guidance amid danger.
meaning: The request joins mercy with a desire to change direction through God’s teaching.

title: A king asks for rescue and flourishing
summary: The speaker praises God’s help in battle. He asks for protection, thriving children, and abundance.
meaning: The desired outcome reaches beyond victory toward households and streets free from distress.

title: Tell later generations about God’s care
summary: The poem praises greatness, compassion, food for creatures, and help for those who fall.
meaning: Lasting kingship appears through care that reaches weak people and all living things.

title: Do not put lasting hope in rulers
summary: The poem contrasts mortal leaders with God. He helps hungry people, prisoners, and those without protection.
meaning: Human plans end with death. The praise identifies care for the overlooked as enduring strength.

title: Praise for renewal, weather, and teaching
summary: The poem describes restored Jerusalem, gathered exiles, healed hearts, and provision for creatures.
meaning: Care for a city and care for the wider world appear within one song.

title: Heaven and earth join the praise
summary: The poem calls stars, weather, animals, rulers, and children to praise the Lord.
meaning: The long invitation places powerful rulers alongside creatures and people of every age.

title: A new song and a call for judgment
summary: The people celebrate with music and then describe armed judgment against nations and kings.
meaning: The ending joins praise with force. Its violent images remain part of the song’s claim.

title: Let everything with breath praise
summary: The final poem calls for praise with horns, strings, drums, dance, and cymbals.
meaning: The collection ends with a wide invitation rather than one person’s prayer.
